title: Light-sail materials surviving gigawatt laser irradiation
bottleneck: Breakthrough Starshot-style missions would push gram-scale sails to a fraction of light speed with ~100-gigawatt laser arrays, but no known material combines the required properties: near-perfect reflectivity at the laser wavelength, near-zero absorption (absorbed energy vaporizes the sail), gram-scale areal density, and tolerance for Doppler-shifted wavelengths as the sail recedes. Metals like gold and silver reflect well but absorb too much to survive; candidates like crystalline silicon and molybdenum disulfide have some right properties but none has the full set.
why_it_blocks: Beamed sails are the only near-term credible path to interstellar flight within a human lifetime; without a survivable sail material, the concept cannot proceed past paper studies.
current_state: Researchers propose nanostructured sails — hexagonal hole lattices, alternating nanometer layers — to boost reflectivity and cut mass, but these remain lab concepts. No sail has flown under anything approaching Starshot-level irradiation.
